The site shape factor: can a site hold the plan's rectangle?

Source: R/shape.R
site_shape_factor.Rd

Some plans require every vacant site created by subdivision to hold a rectangle of a stated size clear of its yards (Auckland Unitary Plan E38.8.1.1(2): 8 m by 15 m, 15 m by 20 m in the Terrace Housing and Apartment Buildings zone). A zone states its rectangle as form$site_shape (width, depth; see building_form()).

Usage

site_shape_factor(x, site_ids = NULL, angle_step = 5, cell = 0.25)

Arguments

x

A scenario().

site_ids

Sites to test. Default: sites in density zones with a rectangle that are at least twice the zone's vacant site minimum (smaller sites count one dwelling whatever their shape).

angle_step

Sweep step of the exact test, degrees.

cell

Raster cell of the exact test, metres.

Value

A data frame, one row per site tested: site_id, rect_width, rect_depth, developable_area, fits, max_lots and decided_by ("area", "rotated_rectangle", "inscribed_disc", "aligned" or "raster").

Details

The rule governs creating vacant sites, so it bears on the subdivision paths only (density, large site, and a hybrid zone taking its density count); estimate_capacity() applies it there. A site that cannot hold one rectangle creates no new site and keeps one dwelling; none creates more sites than its developable area holds rectangles (a necessary bound, not a packing).

The developable area is the site less the zone's yards (each a flat-ended strip along the boundaries it applies to), less water yards and the land exclusion overlays take off.

The test, at any orientation, cheapest first:

  1. it fails if the area is under width x depth, if its minimum rotated rectangle is narrower than the width or shorter than the depth, or if it cannot hold a disc as wide as the rectangle;

  2. it passes if the rectangle fits laid along the minimum rotated rectangle's axes, at its centre or at a point well inside the area;

  3. otherwise it is decided exactly to a grid: the area is rasterised at cell in a frame turned to each of its own edge directions and every angle_step degrees, and a summed-area table asks whether any window of the rectangle's size, either way round, lies wholly inside.

This is stage 1 of capacityengine's design (item 324): a building complying with every zone standard is not also required to fit within the rectangle, and exclusions for which no layer is supplied (hazards, heritage, utilities) are not seen, so the result is optimistic.

Examples

town <- exampleton()
sc <- scenario("Operative", rulebook_example("exampleton"),
               parcels = town$parcels[town$parcels$parcel_type == "land", ],
               roads = town$parcels[town$parcels$parcel_type == "road", ],
               zoning = town$zoning)
head(site_shape_factor(sc))
#> [1] site_id          rect_width       rect_depth       developable_area
#> [5] fits             max_lots         decided_by      
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
